topics.title: Office Management, Filing System, Noting, Drafting & Official Summary Writing
topics.summary: e-FOAS in brief, the five functions of office management, the filing system (opening, register, portions, recording and classification), noting, drafting, summary writing, and the forms of official communication with models.

questions.text: e-FOAS stands for:

options.A: Electronic File Operation and Approval Service

questions.text: e-FOAS was built by:
The stated objective of e-FOAS is to:

options.A: Replace government staff with automated software
options.C: Transform the conventional paper-based government workflow into a secure, paperless digital environment
options.D: Digitise only the dispatch register of each office

questions.text: Under e-FOAS, official record is secured by:

options.B: Duplicate paper files kept in a strong room

questions.text: According to the presentation, e-FOAS has historically cut the government's stationery budget by up to:
e-FOAS generates automated delay alerts when:

options.B: A user logs in from a mobile phone
options.D: A file sits on a desk for too long

questions.text: Why does e-FOAS eliminate "lost" files?

options.A: Record is stored digitally, so misplacement, tampering, hiding or pilfering of files is done away with
options.B: Every file is photocopied three times
options.C: Files are kept with the Secretary personally
options.D: Files are not allowed to move between offices

questions.text: Office management is defined as a technique to achieve efficient and effective performance through:

options.D: Planning, organizing, staffing, directing and controlling

questions.text: According to the presentation, success in office management depends on efficiency, which links with:

options.C: The size of the office building

questions.text: Planning in office management requires:

options.A: Logical thinking, well-founded imagination and sound judgement rather than guesswork
options.D: Waiting for instructions from higher offices

questions.text: Setting up annual activity schedules to achieve goals is part of which function?
Displaying the organizational chart at a conspicuous place and notifying job descriptions of each tier fall under:
"Putting the right person in the right job at the right time" relates to which function?
The principle of unity of command means:

options.A: All officers sign every file jointly
options.B: One department controls all other departments
options.C: Orders are issued only in writing
options.D: An employee has only one supervisor, to avoid confusion

questions.text: According to the presentation, a Director should focus on ______, while a Manager should focus on ______.

options.C: The overall goals of the organization; the tasks he and his team must complete

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT listed as part of directing?

options.A: Giving instructions to subordinates in the right direction
options.C: Motivating employees through communication and coordination
options.D: Framing recruitment rules for the department

questions.text: In controlling, the controller (AD/DG) monitors performance mainly through:

options.C: Visits and surprise visits, teams, committees and other sources

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the listed fallouts (results) of office management?
In the office filing system, a file is:

options.A: Any loose paper received in the office
options.C: A bundle of unrelated papers of one year
options.D: A set of letters and documents on a particular subject, arranged in a proper folder or cover and assigned a number

questions.text: The two main portions of a file are:
Which rule applies when opening a new file?

options.B: One file for all subjects of a year

questions.text: A new file is opened in the:

options.C: File Register, maintained section-wise or branch-wise

questions.text: A file register contains:

options.A: Serial number, subject and file number (with main head and sub-head)
options.D: Pay and allowances of the branch

questions.text: In the specimen file register, the file number DAO/MN/2-4/23 relates to:
The page limit for the correspondence portion of a file is about:
A part file is also known as a:
A linked file is:

options.A: A file sent to the record room
options.B: A file stored only in e-FOAS
options.C: Any other file having related material
options.D: A file opened on the same date

questions.text: Which of the following belongs to the noting portion rather than the correspondence portion?
When arranging papers for a case, which comes first?
Which of the following is NOT a step in recording a file?

options.A: Taking extracts of decisions, orders and advice
options.B: Sending the file to the press for publication
options.C: Ensuring that no further action is required
options.D: Determining the classification of the file

questions.text: Category-A files are:

options.A: Permanent files not to be printed
options.C: Files with a life of 10 to 15 years
options.D: Files with a life of up to 10 years

questions.text: Category-D files have a life of:
PUC stands for:
The abbreviation N.F.A on a file means:
The purpose of noting on a file is to:

options.B: Record the contribution of each tier for future evidence
options.C: Keep the matter secret from senior officers

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT part of the modus operandi for noting?

options.B: Adding personal opinions to strengthen the passage
options.D: Organizing points in a logical order

questions.text: According to the presentation, which draft may be signed and issued?

options.A: Any draft prepared by the dealing clerk
options.B: The first draft, before it is seen by the authority
options.C: Any of several drafts, at the issuer's choice
options.D: Only the finalized draft approved by the authority

questions.text: Among the qualities of good drafting, "correctness" means:

options.A: Using as many words as possible
options.C: Copying the previous draft word for word
options.D: Writing in the passive voice only

questions.text: Among the qualities of an official summary, "objectivity" means:

options.A: Leaving out personal opinions or judgements
options.B: Including the writer's own view on every point
options.C: Reproducing the original text in full

questions.text: An official letter is used for correspondence with:

options.A: Federal or provincial governments, Pakistan missions abroad, foreign missions in Pakistan, the High Court, public bodies and individuals
options.B: Only subordinate offices of the same department
options.C: Only the Finance Department, for advice
options.D: Only officers, for their personal attention

questions.text: A memorandum is used for correspondence:

options.B: With the general public through the press
options.C: With subordinate or equal-status offices within the same government, and between Secretariat departments

questions.text: A demi-official (D.O.) letter is used:

options.A: To publish rules in the official gazette
options.B: Between government officers, to draw personal attention for expeditious disposal of pending issues
options.C: To transfer officials of Grade 15 and below
options.D: To give wide publicity to government policy

questions.text: An un-official (U.O.) letter is mainly used for:

options.A: Appointment of officers of Grade 16 and above
options.B: Interdepartmental reference for information or advice, particularly to the Finance Department
options.D: Sending a copy to additional addressees

questions.text: Appointments, postings and transfers of officers of Grade 16 and above are issued through a:
An office order is used for:

options.A: Publishing ordinances and bills in the gazette
options.B: Postings of officers of Grade 16 and above
options.C: Appointments, promotions, leave and similar matters of subordinate staff; its scope is restricted
options.D: Interdepartmental advice from the Finance Department

questions.text: An endorsement is used when:

options.A: A file is closed and sent to the record room
options.B: A draft is returned for correction
options.C: An officer is given additional charge
options.D: A copy of a communication is to be sent to others in addition to the original addressee

questions.text: A press communique or press release is issued:

options.A: To give wide publicity to a government decision or policy through the press/DGPR, with the approval of the Minister-in-charge
options.B: To convey a decision only to the officer concerned
options.D: To seek advice from another department

questions.text: In a D.O. letter, the salutation "My dear Sir" is used when writing to:
In the model noting, references such as "PUC at page 10-11/C" and "Para 2/N" mean:

options.B: Pages of the correspondence portion and a paragraph of the noting portion
options.C: Chapter 10 of the rules and note 2 of the manual

questions.text: In the model summary for the Chief Minister, the Secretary seeks authority to sign the Order of Inquiry on the CM's behalf under:

topics.title: PEEDA Act 2006 & Conducting Departmental Inquiries
topics.summary: Evolution from the E&D Rules and PRSO 2000, definitions, grounds and the 14 penalties, competent authorities, the procedure in sections 5 to 26, time limits, allied laws, natural justice, conducting an inquiry, why orders are set aside, and case studies.

questions.text: The PEEDA Act 2006 is Act ______ of 2006, published in the Punjab Gazette on ______.
Section 26 of the PEEDA Act 2006 repealed the:

options.A: Punjab Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance 2000

questions.text: Section 2 of PEEDA contains how many definitions?
PEEDA provides 14 penalties in total. How are they divided?
Under s.2(f)(ii), an officer authorised by the Chief Minister to act as competent authority must not be inferior in rank to:

options.C: The appointing authority prescribed for the post held by the accused

questions.text: Where two or more employees are proceeded against jointly, the competent authority for all of them is:

options.A: The competent authority of the junior-most accused
options.B: The Chief Minister in every case
options.C: The competent authority of the senior-most accused

questions.text: If a competent authority (other than the CM) has an interest in the result of the proceedings, it must:

options.A: Not proceed, and report the matter to the next higher authority, who authorises another officer of corresponding rank
options.B: Proceed, but record its interest on file
options.C: Hand the case to the inquiry officer to decide
options.D: Close the case for want of an authority

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the six limbs of "corruption" under s.2(g)?

options.A: Having a reputation of being corrupt
options.B: Failing a departmental examination three times

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT benami, according to the presentation?

options.A: A house in the driver's name, paid for and lived in by the officer
options.B: A plot in a jobless son's name, bought with cash deposited a week earlier
options.C: A car registered to the peon but used and paid for by the officer
options.D: A flat in the officer's wife's name, bought from her own declared inheritance

questions.text: What is the key test for identifying a benamidar?

options.A: The source of the money: who actually paid
options.B: Whose name appears on the registry
options.D: Whether the property was bought in cash

questions.text: An official sells flour from the ration store and shows it as "consumed". Under the presentation's classification, this is:

options.A: Dishonest misappropriation of property found by chance
options.B: Misuse of government property that is later returned
options.D: Embezzlement (breach of trust over property entrusted to the post)

questions.text: Under s.2(k), "inefficiency" includes failure to qualify the departmental examination in:
After the 2012 amendment, the definition of "employee" in s.2(h)(ii) does NOT include:

options.B: Judges and employees of the Lahore High Court and its subordinate courts, and employees of Police
options.C: Employees of tribunals set up by the Government
options.D: Holders of civil posts in the province

questions.text: Acquittal by a court as a result of compounding an offence involving moral turpitude or affecting the human body is treated under PEEDA as:
Section 3 of PEEDA provides how many grounds for proceedings?

options.B: Four: inefficiency, misconduct, corruption, and subversion/disclosure of official secrets
options.D: Five: adding absence from duty as a separate ground

questions.text: The minor penalty of fine may not exceed:
The minor penalties of withholding increments and reduction to lower stages are capped at:
Which of the following is a MAJOR penalty under s.4(1)(b)?

options.B: Withholding of promotion for up to five years
options.C: Fine up to one month's basic pay
options.D: Forfeiture of past service for up to five years

questions.text: What distinguishes dismissal from removal from service?

options.B: Dismissal disqualifies the employee from future government employment (s.4(2)); removal does not
options.C: Dismissal can only be imposed on retired employees
options.D: There is no difference under PEEDA

questions.text: According to the Guidebook cautions, compulsory retirement may be imposed only if the accused has:
Where charges of grave corruption are proved, the law requires:

options.C: Dismissal from service, in addition to recovery, if any
options.D: Any penalty the competent authority thinks fit

questions.text: Where absence from duty for more than one year is proved, the penalty must be:

options.B: Recovery of pay for the period of absence
options.C: Compulsory retirement, removal or dismissal from service
options.D: Censure and treating the period as leave without pay

questions.text: The duty to pass a reasoned (speaking) order and supply a copy to the person affected comes from:

options.C: Section 24-A of the Punjab General Clauses Act 1956

questions.text: Under the PMS Rules 2004, the appointing authority for a BS-18 PMS officer is the:
For a retired government employee, the competent authority under PEEDA is (S&GAD notification of 06.02.2007):

options.B: The appointing authority at the time of retirement
options.C: The current head of the employee's last office

questions.text: A hearing officer may be appointed only where the competent authority is of the rank of:

options.B: Secretary to the Government of the Punjab or above
options.D: Any rank, if the accused agrees

questions.text: When an employee on deputation holds a post in BS-17 or above, the borrowing organisation must:

options.A: Return the employee before any inquiry
options.B: Seek approval of the Service Tribunal
options.C: Obtain prior approval of the lending organisation before taking action under PEEDA
options.D: Proceed without informing the lending organisation

questions.text: Under the proviso to s.5(1)(a), no show cause or personal hearing is given in which case?

options.A: The employee is a BS-19 officer
options.B: The employee has applied for leave
options.C: The employee has been posted to another district
options.D: The employee has entered into a plea bargain, or been convicted of corruption

questions.text: Under the proviso to s.5(1)(b), the competent authority SHALL dispense with the inquiry where the employee:

options.B: Has a long, clean service record
options.C: Has been convicted of an offence other than corruption, or has been absent from duty without prior approval of leave
options.D: Is due to retire within a year

questions.text: Under s.6, suspension is initially for 90 days. If it is not extended within 30 days of expiry of that period, the employee:

options.A: Stays suspended until the inquiry ends
options.C: Must apply to the Service Tribunal

questions.text: Under PEEDA, the accused gets how long to submit a written defence or reply to a show cause notice?

options.A: Seven days (or any extended period the competent authority allows)

questions.text: After receiving the inquiry report, the competent authority (other than the CM) must decide the case within:
In the show-cause route under s.7, the competent authority must decide the case within ______ of receiving the reply.
Under s.10(6), the inquiry officer must submit the report within 60 days. If the deadline is missed:

options.A: The inquiry is not vitiated merely because the time schedule was not observed
options.D: The inquiry officer is liable to dismissal

questions.text: Are the inquiry officer's recommendations binding on the competent authority?

options.D: Only where the CM is the competent authority

questions.text: The inquiry officer must hear the case day to day. An adjournment may be granted only:

options.A: For reasons recorded in writing, and for not more than seven days
options.B: On the accused's oral request, for any period

questions.text: Under s.11(2), PEEDA inquiry proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings within the meaning of:

options.B: Sections 193 and 228 of the Pakistan Penal Code 1860

questions.text: Giving false evidence before an inquiry officer (s.193 PPC) is punishable with imprisonment of up to:
The departmental representative is appointed in the order of inquiry:

options.A: By name, chosen by the accused
options.D: Only when the accused asks for one

questions.text: A departmental appeal under s.16 must be filed within ______ of communication of the order. If the CM imposed the penalty, the remedy is ______.

options.A: 60 days; an appeal to the Chief Secretary
options.C: 30 days; a review petition to the CM
options.D: 15 days; a revision to the Governor

questions.text: Revision under s.17 may be exercised within ______ of the order, by ______.

options.D: One year; the CM, Chief Secretary, Administrative Secretary or any other appellate authority

questions.text: Under s.18, the accused may be represented by an advocate:

options.A: Only in proceedings before the Punjab Service Tribunal (s.19)
options.B: At every stage of the proceedings

questions.text: If the appellate authority does not decide a departmental appeal within 60 days, the employee may appeal to the Punjab Service Tribunal within:

options.A: 30 days of filing the departmental appeal
options.B: One year of the original order
options.D: 90 days of filing the departmental appeal

questions.text: Which employees cannot appeal to the Punjab Service Tribunal under s.19?

options.B: Employees of corporations and autonomous bodies covered by s.2(h)(i)

questions.text: For a retired employee, PEEDA proceedings must be initiated within ______ of retirement and finalised within ______ of retirement.
According to the presentation, a probe (fact-finding) should be held before framing charges when:

options.A: The offence and the offender are both known
options.C: The offence or the offender (or both) is not known
options.D: The accused is a retired employee

questions.text: What standard of proof applies in a departmental inquiry?
The maxims "audi alteram partem" and "nemo judex in causa sua" mean, respectively:

options.A: Hear the other side; no one should be a judge in their own cause
options.B: Let the buyer beware; the law does not concern itself with trifles
options.D: By the fact itself; from the beginning

questions.text: Under the CrPC (s.225), an error or omission in a charge is material only if:

options.A: The charge has a spelling mistake
options.B: The charge was typed rather than handwritten
options.C: The inquiry took more than 60 days
options.D: The accused was in fact misled and it caused a failure of justice

questions.text: Among the fatal flaws identified by the S&GAD letter of 10.09.2014, a competent authority that disagrees with the inquiry officer must:

options.A: Simply impose a higher penalty without notice
options.B: Record reasons for differing, and state the proposed penalty in the show cause notice
options.C: Send the case to the Service Tribunal
options.D: Appoint the same inquiry officer again without reasons

glossary.full: Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability (Act 2006)
Punjab Removal from Service (Special Powers) Ordinance 2000
